title: Iqbal Ahmad v. State of U.P. And 2 Others
coram: Naheed Ara Moonis, J. & Dinesh Pathak, J.
disposition: Writ petition disposed of without deciding merits; petitioner to file a representation within two weeks for a reasoned speaking final assessment after hearing, preferably within four weeks; coercive action stayed for six weeks or until that decision, whichever is earlier; no benefit if the representation is not filed
headnote: A licensee cannot recover by treating a provisional assessment as the final assessment without an opportunity of hearing and without supplying a copy of a final order. Applying Shishir Jain, the Division Bench held that the consumer cannot be compelled to deposit the provisional figure unless a final assessment is made after considering the objection and hearing him. Treating the provisional amount as final is dehors Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clauses 6.8 and 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and violates natural justice; Clause 8.1 requires inspection, provisional assessment, hearing and final assessment in theft cases. Without entering the merits, the Court directed a fresh representation for a reasoned speaking final assessment after hearing, stayed coercive action on the recovery for six weeks or until that decision, and withheld the benefit of the order if the representation is not filed. The assessment and recovery notices were not quashed.
facts:
Iqbal Ahmad petitioned the Allahabad High Court to quash recovery of Rs. 1,09,612 against service connection No. 2313118648, founded on Assessment Cum Recovery Notice No. 2638 dated 16 September 2019 and demand notices dated 31 December 2019 under Sections 3 and 5 of the U.P. Government Electrical Undertaking (Dues Recovery) Act, 1958. He said a checking report dated 25 August 2019 found no irregularity at the premises, whereas the provisional notice recited an inspection on 14 September 2019; the provisional figure was then treated as the final assessment and a recovery citation issued without a hearing, contrary to Section 126(3) of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clauses 6.8 and 8.1 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.

Counsel for the Power Corporation (respondents 2 and 3) said inspection found use of electricity by illegal means; a provisional assessment notice issued on 16 September 2019; and as no objection was filed, that notice was treated as the final assessment.

holding_units.clause: 8.1 (theft — inspection, provisional assessment, hearing and final assessment)
holding_units.topic: Provisional theft assessment cannot be treated as final without hearing and supply of the order
holding_units.question: May a licensee recover a theft demand by treating a provisional assessment as final because no objection was filed, without a hearing and without supplying a copy of a final order?
holding_units.holding: No. Applying Shishir Jain, the petitioner could not be compelled to deposit on the provisional assessment without an opportunity of hearing while making a final assessment, and without being supplied a copy of that order. Treating the provisional amount as final without a hearing is dehors Section 126 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and Clauses 6.8 and 8.1 of the Code, 2005, and violates natural justice. Clause 8.1 is the licensee's procedure for inspection, provisional assessment, hearing and final assessment in theft of electricity. Without entering the merits, the Court directed a representation within two weeks for a reasoned speaking final assessment after hearing, preferably within four weeks; coercive action on the recovery is stayed for six weeks or until that decision, whichever is earlier; default in filing the representation forfeits the benefit. The notices were not quashed.
holding_units.qualifier: Operative relief is a time-bound representation, not certiorari. The Court cited Clause 6.8 alongside Clause 8.1 without choosing between unauthorised use and theft.
holding_units.flag: Unnumbered 2.2.2021 order; paras are sequential blocks after the cause-title (1 heard; 2 reliefs; 3 petitioner's facts including the 25.8.2019 checking report vs 14.9.2019 inspection; 4 petitioner's 126(3)/6.8/8.1 and no-hearing case; 5 licensee's illegal-means / no-objection reply; 6 Shishir Jain para 16 quoted; 7 procedure dehors s.126 and Clauses 6.8 and 8.1, Clause 8.1 described as the theft path, natural justice; 8 representation directed without entering merits; 9 coercive action stayed; 10 no benefit if representation not filed). Catalog hits on Clauses 2.2, 4.3, 4.35–4.39 and 8.14 are false positives.

holding_units.topic: No deposit can be compelled on a provisional Section 126 assessment without a final assessment after hearing
holding_units.question: Can a consumer be compelled to deposit a provisionally assessed amount when no final assessment after hearing has been made or supplied?
holding_units.holding: No. Following Shishir Jain paragraph 16, without a final assessment after considering the objection and giving an opportunity of hearing, the consumer cannot be compelled to deposit any amount. The procedure adopted by respondent no. 3 was held dehors Section 126. The writ court did not itself make or quash an assessment; it sent the matter back for a speaking final assessment after hearing.
holding_units.qualifier: Petitioner invoked Section 126(3); the Court's own holding is framed as Section 126. The recovery notices were not quashed.

holding_units.topic: Clause 6.8 cited as also violated; not separately construed
holding_units.holding: The petitioner invoked Clause 6.8 together with Clause 8.1 and Section 126(3). The Court held the procedure dehors Clause 6.8 as well as Clause 8.1 and Section 126, but identified Clause 8.1 as the theft-assessment procedure and did not separately construe Clause 6.8.
holding_units.flag: Both 6.8 and 8.1 were named; the Court did not decide whether the demand was unauthorised use or theft.

principle_tags.application: The Court would not let recovery of Rs. 1,09,612 stand as concluded where the 16.9.2019 provisional assessment was treated as final without a hearing or supply of a final order; a representation for a speaking final assessment after hearing was directed.

principle_tags.application: Clause 8.1 was applied as the theft path requiring inspection, provisional assessment, hearing and final assessment; treating the provisional figure as final without hearing was held to violate that procedure and natural justice.

principle_tags.application: Applying Shishir Jain paragraph 16, the Court held that without a final assessment after considering the objection and granting a hearing, the petitioner could not be compelled to deposit the provisional amount under Section 126.

principle_tags.application: The licensee had treated the 16.9.2019 provisional notice as final because no objection was filed; recovery on that basis was held unsustainable until a hearing and a final assessment, and coercive action was stayed.

principle_tags.application: The amount in the 16.9.2019 provisional assessment-cum-recovery notice was treated as the final assessment without a hearing; that course was held dehors Clause 8.1 and Section 126.

authorities.name: Shishir Jain v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and another
authorities.proposition: If there is no final assessment, the consumer cannot be compelled to deposit the amount of the provisional assessment; without a final assessment after considering the objection and giving an opportunity of hearing, notices demanding that amount are unsustainable (para 16).
